parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction. The operative documented feature is an unenforced sodomy statute (14-year maximum, no arrests or prosecutions recorded 2010–2013 or in recent advocacy assessment) — a secondary, sexuality-law signal that is a dead letter on paper but sits atop a rule-of-law-weak state (lengthy pretrial detention, corruption) and elite moral hostility (2017, 2018 official statements condemning legal change, citing scripture). No trans-specific data exists on documents, facilities, policing, detention or violence; extrapolation from structure — criminalised conduct, no non-discrimination protection, no recognition, official opposition to reform, dropped constitutional protections — resolves toward risk, not neutrality, but the absence of any documented targeting or enforcement keeps it out of the organised-targeting tiers. Latent statute plus hostile elite framing plus thin recourse sits at the upper Elevated band.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No sourced information on entry practice, passport marker scrutiny or visa rules; whether officers accept foreign markers is an open question.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown entry screening could out a traveller; with no record of adverse outcomes, this is an open question, not an exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: General rule-of-law weakness documented: lengthy pretrial detention and corruption. The sodomy statute carries 14 years but no prosecutions are recorded; placement practice for trans detainees is unknown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If ever invoked, a weak judiciary with deference to police would offer little remedy; custody exposure is structural extrapolation, not documented practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No sourced information on bathrooms, wards, shelters or single-sex spaces.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No non-discrimination protection covering gender identity is documented — a resident-facing gap, not a traveller exposure.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility placement if detained or hospitalised is unresolved; thin-data extrapolation cannot confirm safety.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No information on medication import, refills, or care access for trans visitors.
care_services.interaction: Care refusal upon discovery is an unanswered question; no evidence either way.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Elite moral framing documented: head-of-state representative warning same-sex marriage 'cannot populate the world' (2018), PM opposition (2017), scripture-inflected condemnation of reform. This is hostility to recognition and change, not documented targeting of trans people; police enforcement against LGBT people is absent from the record.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None documented; reform proposals rejected (2008), UN pledge not to decriminalise (2011), constitutional protection dropped in successive drafts.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility signals a climate in which any police interaction could escalate, but no lever documented as actually used.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific data on minors or travelling families; the criminal statute concerns consensual adult conduct, not minors' presentation.
minors_guardians.interaction: None sourced; an adult travelling with a minor faces the same undocumented axes as a solo adult, with no additional documented layer.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence documented; general violence against women prevalent (2013). Reference notes LGBT people face 'legal challenges not experienced by other residents' — a thin social-climate signal, not a violence pattern.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented; absence of reported abuse in 2011–2013 foreign reports is weak evidence in a thin-data state.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Whether police protect an outed trans victim is unknown; general corruption and weak institutions suggest no reliable recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Key unknowns: document practice at entry, custody placement, facility access, care access, current enforcement status post-2013. No domestic prosecution figures exist.
remedies_unknowns.protection: No working remedy documented; no anti-discrimination law, no relief record.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin data plus criminalisation plus no recourse resolves toward the structural risk implied, not the midpoint.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A documents an active, universal visitor-facing exposure: a conduct register with routine border enforcement and no remedy. This dossier documents no enforcement of any kind — only an unenforced statute and hostile rhetoric. That is materially less exposure, placing this jurisdiction above the 0.35 tier despite thin data.

0.55-B shows recurring, documented administrative exposure at borders (secondary screening, refused entry) with working but slow appeals. Here no traveller-facing exposure is documented at all, but the criminal statute, elite hostility, weak institutions and absent recourse keep it below that tier; 0.45 sits between this and the enforcement anchors.

0.75-C has documented protective machinery: trained officers, a functioning tribunal, compensation for unlawful detention. This dossier documents no protections actually operating, no acceptance evidence, and a latent 14-year statute in a weak-rule-of-law state with officially hostile leadership — well below that tier.

0.25-C documents repeated custody harm: birth-sex prison housing, assaults, arrests under a cross-dressing statute. This dossier documents no arrests, no custody practice, and a sexuality statute that is a dead letter — the secondary factor alone cannot support that tier's weight here.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a national framework whose only documented trans-relevant legal feature is a latent, unenforced sodomy statute with a 14-year maximum — a secondary signal the record shows unused, with foreign reporting (2010–2013) and advocacy assessment both recording no prosecutions. Layered on it: elite officials publicly hostile to any recognition of sexual or gender minorities, successive withdrawal of constitutional protections, a stated refusal to decriminalise, no non-discrimination shield, and general institutional weakness. No trans-specific data exists on any traveller axis — documents, facilities, custody, care, policing, violence — so the rating rests on structural extrapolation: a state that criminalises same-sex conduct, offers no recognition or recourse, and whose leadership frames the minority as a moral problem, but which shows no documented pattern of enforcement or targeting. That places the traveller's exposure at social and latent-legal risk with thin remedy, above documented-enforcement regimes (0.25–0.35) but well below jurisdictions with documented protections or acceptance (0.65+).
